articleTitle: A Compact Design of High-Gain Phased Array Antenna for THz and 6G Communication Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Future Telecommunications and Artificial Intelligence (IC-FTAI)
abstract: This paper explores the characteristics of an innovative linear phased array designed to provide high gain and steerable radiation patterns, tailored to meet the demands of upcoming 6G networks. The array features a schematic with eight modified dipole elements arranged in a 1×8 linear format. To improve the radiation efficiency of the dipole resonators, rectangular directors are strategically placed adjacent to each resonator. These compact resonators utilize microstrip-line feeds, optimizing their design. The proposed phased array achieves an impedance bandwidth of 1.85 to 2.15 THz at −10 dB, delivering radiation gains exceeding 12 dBi across various angles. This performance meets the requirements for 6G communications.

articleTitle: Dual-Band MIMO Antenna with S-Shaped Monopole Resonators for 2.5/3.5 THz 6G Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Future Telecommunications and Artificial Intelligence (IC-FTAI)
abstract: This study presents a 4-element MIMO antenna array designed for THz and 6G communications. The antenna features a straightforward design, utilizing low-profile S-shaped monopole elements fed by microstrip lines, positioned on different sides of a compact board with overall dimensions of 13 x 13 μm, The proposed MIMO antenna demonstrates dual-band functionality, operating effectively at 2.5 THz and 3.5 THz. The array shows strong potential in terms of key performance metrics, including S-parameters, radiation patterns, and gain/efficiency levels, making it a promising candidate for future networks.

articleTitle: Time-Modulated of Fractal Sierpinski Carpet Array with Reduced Sidelobe levels
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Future Telecommunications and Artificial Intelligence (IC-FTAI)
abstract: In this paper, fractal Sierpinski carpet array with reduced side lobe levels (SLL) is redesigned using the time-modulation technique. Circular-curl antenna element is used for circular polarization. The method of moment is used to calculate the radiation characteristics of the array. The particle swarm algorithm (PSO) is used to optimize the on-time instant and the on-time duration. The side lobe levels have been reduced to more than -22.5 dB. The multiband operation capabilities and the beam width of the main beam remain unchanged.

articleTitle: A Broadband MIMO Antenna Array with Low-Profile Slit Resonators for Sub-6-GHz 5G Mobile Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Future Telecommunications and Artificial Intelligence (IC-FTAI)
abstract: This study presents an 8×8 multiple-input, multiple-output (MIMO) antenna array specifically designed to meet the demands of 5G cellular handheld devices. The antenna features a distinctive configuration, utilizing low-profile inverted T-shaped slits that are fed by rectangular microstrip lines arranged in two rows on opposite sides of the board (four resonators on each side). The investigated MIMO antenna array offers a broadband impedance bandwidth with dual-resonance functionality, operating efficiently from 3.4 GHz to 4.2 GHz. The design delivers excellent performance in key characteristics such as S-parameters, efficiency, gain levels, and radiation patterns. In addition, the configuration of the CPW-fed resonators allows the proposed design to function as two distinct beam-steerable arrays, delivering high-gain radiation at various angles, thus making it suitable for deployment in 5G cellular networks.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Soft Robot Based on Fluidic Elastomer Actuators
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Future Telecommunications and Artificial Intelligence (IC-FTAI)
abstract: Soft robotics is an affluent research topic nowa- days with the increased need for robots able to adapt to changing environments. Fluidic elastomer actuators, composed of embedded chambers in a hyper-elastic material with a fluid acting as a resistive variable, are one of the most promising actuators in soft robotics. However, there are still design and modeling challenges that hinder its behavior prediction and wide spread in applications. For instance, the need for improving the reconfigurability concept by connecting different actuator segments taking into consideration its geometric parameters, material properties and actuation method. In the proposed study we present a soft robot reconfigurable modular design approach integrating more than one soft robot modular actuator segment that can be adjusted to create different robot configurations. Additionally, the simulation results offer valuable insights into the system's behavior, including its motion and strain, both in standalone and combined configurations, as analyzed through Finite Element Analysis (FEA).

articleTitle: Optimizing Medical Image Classification: Leveraging Advanced Segmentation Models for Enhanced Object Detection in Real-World Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Future Telecommunications and Artificial Intelligence (IC-FTAI)
abstract: In medical imaging, classifiers typically rely on objects of interest, such as nodules, being centered and fully visible within the frame to effectively learn the underlying relationships necessary for accurate classification. However, in real-world scenarios, such conditions are not always met, leading to challenges in classification accuracy. This paper explores the enhancement of classifier performance by incorporating advanced segmentation models, including SAM, SAM2, and Dinov2, all of which are pretrained for automatic semantic segmentation. We compare the results of integrating these modelsto preprocess and segment medical images, thereby improving the classifier's ability to correctly identify and classify objectsin non-ideal conditions. The study aims to demonstrate how leveraging state-of-the-art segmentation techniques can bridge the gap between idealized assumptions and real-world medical data, ultimately leading to more robust and accurate classificationoutcomes.

articleTitle: Analysis and Mitigation of Phase Noise Effects in Linear Frequency Modulated Radar Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Future Telecommunications and Artificial Intelligence (IC-FTAI)
abstract: Phase noise presents a significant challenge in mod-ern radar systems, particularly those employing Linear frequency Modulation (LFM) waveforms. This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of phase noise effects on radar per-formance and evaluates various mitigation strategies. Through detailed simulation studies, we quantify the impact of phase noise levels ranging from 0 to 0.5 radians on Peak-to-Sidelobe Ra-tio (PSLR) performance. Results demonstrate significant PSLR degradation from −60.6 dB under ideal conditions to −32.7 dB under severe phase noise conditions. We implement and compare three mitigation techniques: window functions, phase compensation, and coherent integration. The coherent integration method proves most effective, achieving a 27.5 dB improvement in PSLR compared to uncompensated signals. Our analysis provides practical insights into phase noise mitigation strategies and their relative effectiveness, contributing to the development of more robust radar systems. The methodology and results presented offer valuable guidelines for radar system designers in selecting and implementing appropriate phase noise mitigation techniques based on specific performance requirements. Our analysis demonstrates a 27.5 dB improvement in PSLR compared to uncompensated signals, outperforming previous methods which achieved improvements of 15–20 dB

articleTitle: Speed Sign Detection Using Computer Vision Techniques in ADAS Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Future Telecommunications and Artificial Intelligence (IC-FTAI)
abstract: Traffic sign detection is one of the most important modules in Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) that help to improve road-safety. In this paper, the real-time traffic sign detection system is proposed based on a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model implemented in Python. The system identifies and classifies traffic signs in video feeds while handling variations in object size. By convolutional layers, feature extraction was optimized to improve the detection of small and occluded signs. A special loss function is also used to enhance the accuracy of bounding box regression. Much testing on a real-life traffic sign dataset exhibits that the system reaches the best accuracy of 97%, which remarkably reduces detection under challenging conditions with a low miss rate and high overall accuracy.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning Framework Based on Novel Hierarchical-LSTM Model for Enhanced Machinery Prognostics
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Future Telecommunications and Artificial Intelligence (IC-FTAI)
abstract: Machinery prognostics has garnered increasing research attention due to its critical role in industries such as manufacturing and renewable energy. Data-driven techniques, particularly recurrent neural networks (RNNs) and convolutional neural networks (CNNs), have shown promise in accurately extracting features for estimating the remaining useful life (RUL) of machinery. However, the non-stationary and non-linear nature of machinery signals poses significant challenges to achieving accurate prognostics. This study introduces a novel hierarchical recurrent neural network method called hierarchical long short-term memory (H-LSTM) that is based on the long short-term memory (LSTM) model. H-LSTM is meant to address the problems with traditional RNNs that only use the previous time step for sequential data learning. It incorporates a hierarchical structure, enabling influence from multiple preceding time steps at each current step. Experimental evaluation on the FEMTO benchmark bearing dataset under varying operational conditions demonstrates that the proposed H-LSTM approach achieves up to fourfold improvements in performance compared to state-of-the-art methods, particularly for low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) signals.

articleTitle: Microstrip-Fed Monopole Antenna with Dual Notch Bands and Ultra-Wideband Characteristics for Wireless Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Future Telecommunications and Artificial Intelligence (IC-FTAI)
abstract: This study unveils a new ultra-wideband (UWB) antenna design that incorporates a dual band-notched feature for enhanced wireless communication. The design includes a trapezoidal radiation patch adorned with two rotated T-shaped slits, a modified rectangular feeding line with an inverted U-shaped slot, and a trapezoidal grounding plane. The performance results demonstrate that the antenna operates over a wide frequency range from 2.8 to 12.5 GHz, encompassing the entire UWB spectrum from 3.1 to 10.6 GHz. A key highlight of this antenna is its dual band-notched functionality, specifically at 3.8 GHz (covering 3.3-4.2 GHz) and 5.5 GHz (spanning 5–6 GHz), designed to effectively avoid interference from WLAN, C-band, and WiMAX frequencies. The study rigorously assesses the investigated antenna, confirming its capability to deliver satisfactory frequency responses, radiation patterns, as well as efficiency and gain levels as per the intended design. The suggested antenna system successfully meets the stringent requirements for band notched UWB communications, underscoring its potential for seamless integration into modern wireless networks.

articleTitle: MIMO Smartphone Antenna with Compact Hook-Shaped Monopole Elements for 5G Handheld Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Future Telecommunications and Artificial Intelligence (IC-FTAI)
abstract: The increasing need for multi-port MIMO antennas, driven largely by the advancements in technologies like 5G networks, has highlighted a significant area of research. This paper introduces an innovative design for a MIMO antenna, specifically tailored for applications in the sub-6 GHz frequency bands, which are critical for the 5G cellular communications. The design features discrete-fed inverted hook-shaped monopole resonators, a choice that provides excellent characteristics for such applications. The uniqueness of the antenna design is further emphasized by its configuration, which includes eight hook-shaped resonators onto the same layer as the ground. This design choice allows the antenna to operate within the 3.4 to 3.6 GHz, matching the requirements for sub-6 GHz communications.

articleTitle: A New Design of MIMO Smartphone Antenna Array for 3.6 GHz Cellular Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Future Telecommunications and Artificial Intelligence (IC-FTAI)
abstract: The growing demand for multi-port MIMO antennas, largely fueled by advancements in technologies such as 5G networks, has underscored an important area of research. This paper presents a novel MIMO antenna design, specifically optimized for use in the sub-6 GHz frequency bands, which are essential for 5G cellular communications. The design incorporates discrete-fed modified monopole resonators etched onto the same layer as the ground. The antenna elements consist of a hook-shaped monopole coupled with an L-shaped strip, enabling operation within the 3.3 to 4 GHz range, aligning with the requirements for sub-6 GHz cellular applications.

articleTitle: Enhancing Dental Caries Detection with YOLOv9: A Comprehensive Analysis and Validation of an Automated Object Detection Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Future Telecommunications and Artificial Intelligence (IC-FTAI)
abstract: This study presents the development and validation of an advanced object detection model based on YOLOv9 for the automated identification of dental caries. Utilizing a dataset of 270 dental images sourced from Kaggle, this proj ect introduces a methodological framework that includes image preprocessing, augmentation, and annotation to address the challenge of limited data. The dataset was expanded through augmentation techniques such as flipping, rotation, shearing, and noise addition, resulting in a final dataset size that supports robust model training and evaluation. Employing the YOLOv9 model, known for its speed and accuracy, we conducted extensive training, optimization, and validation processes. Our results showcase a significant improvement in model performance, with a mean Average Precision (mAP) increase from 59.6% to 93.485%, alongside substantial gains in precision, recall, and F1 scores for detecting dental caries. This study not only highlights the effectiveness of YOLOv9 in dental anomaly detection but also sets a precedent for employing advanced object detection models in medical imaging analysis, offering potential enhancements in diagnostic accuracy and efficiency.

articleTitle: A Compact Phased Array with Bow-Tie Resonators for Terahertz and 6G Wireless Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Future Telecommunications and Artificial Intelligence (IC-FTAI)
abstract: To fulfill the sophisticated requirements of forthcoming networks, phased arrays must possess broadband capability, along with extensive scanning and end-fire radiation properties. This study delves into a new design that integrates low-profile super wide band resonators, specifically crafted for cutting-edge 6G telecommunications. The design approach is straightforward, allowing for easy implementation on the circuit boards of future mobile devices. It features eight bow-tie dipole resonators organized in a single row (1 x8 linear configuration), covering an extensive frequency range from 1.65 to 2.55 THz at a -10 dB threshold. This allows the design to encompass various bands within the 5G and upcoming 6G spectrums. The phased array design is not only easy to execute but also aligns with the complex needs of next-generation wireless technologies, showcasing its potential to enhance future communication systems.

articleTitle: Monopole Antenna Design with Dual Notch Bands and Ultra-Wideband properties for Wireless Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Future Telecommunications and Artificial Intelligence (IC-FTAI)
abstract: This research introduces a novel ultra-wideband (UWB) antenna design featuring dual band-notched function. The antenna's architecture comprises a trapezoid radiation patch, a modified rectangular feedline with a rotated E-shaped strip, and a trapezoid ground plane with a pair of rectangular slits. The obtained results highlight the antenna's operational range from 3 to 13 GHz, effectively covering the UWB spectrum. Particularly noteworthy are the dual band-notched characteristics achieved at 3.8 GHz and 5.5 GHz, strategically implemented to mitigate interference from WLAN, C-band, and WiMAX systems. The study rigorously assesses the investigated antenna, confirming its capability to deliver satisfactory frequency responses, radiation patterns, as well as efficiency and gain levels as per the intended design. In summary, the suggested modified antenna design successfully meets the stringent requirements for band-notched UWB wireless communications, underscoring its potential for seamless integration into modern wireless networks.

articleTitle: A Miniature Radar for Critical Mission Application
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Future Telecommunications and Artificial Intelligence (IC-FTAI)
abstract: In this paper, we present a prototype of a miniature radar system using the ESP32 microcontroller and an HC-SR04 ultrasonic sensor. The prototype utilizes a servo motor to rotate the ultrasonic sensor across a 180-degree arc to mimic the functionality of traditional radar systems. The prototype enables the radar to scan and detect objects and support applications in autonomous vehicle navigation, monitoring, and proximity detection in smart home systems. The prototype highlights the adaptability of the ESP32 and ultrasonic technology in creating cost-effective, scalable, and efficient radar-like systems.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of LCMV Beamforming for GNSS Anti-Spoofing in Multiple Interference Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Future Telecommunications and Artificial Intelligence (IC-FTAI)
abstract: This paper presents an implementation of Linearly Constrained Minimum Variance (LCMV) beamforming for mitigating Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) spoofing attacks. The proposed method utilizes an antenna array to spatially filter spoofing signals while preserving authentic satellite signals. We demonstrate that by exploiting the spatial diversity of authentic satellite signals and the co-located nature of spoofing signals, LCMV beamforming can effectively suppress spoofing interference while maintaining authentic signal reception. Simulation results show spoofing signal suppression of up to −312 dB while maintaining authentic signal reception at −16 dB relative to peak gain.

articleTitle: Multimodal Machine Learning for Evidence Base Medicine
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Future Telecommunications and Artificial Intelligence (IC-FTAI)
abstract: Practicing evidence-based medicine relies on identifying related evidences like medical literature or clinical trial which include credible information related to the clinical case where such evidence typically contains imaging and non-imaging data. However, classical machine learning techniques rely on using monomodal learning that process only a single modality (e.g. text, images or videos). Although this type of learning has provided extraordinary results in clinical science including diagnosis and prognosis, it has limited usage capabilities related to precision and evidence-based medicine. Multimodal learning, however, utilizes techniques to process and find relationships between different types of data modalities to comprehend the case description as some clinical cues exist only in certain modalities. Actually in clinical practice, clinicians use imaging modalities like computed tomography (CT) scans or X-ray images beside non-image modalities like electroencephalogram (EEG) data or tabular data used in the electronic healthcare records to describe clinical cases. In this article we are presenting a multimodal machine framework that can be used for evidence-based practice using fine tuned MedCLIP transformer model to fetch relevant PubMed articles based on three different scenarios of usage where clinicians can provide multimodal queries in their search for relevant PubMed articles.

articleTitle: A Double-Fed Slot Antenna with WLAN Band Filtering and Polarization Diversity for UWB Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Future Telecommunications and Artificial Intelligence (IC-FTAI)
abstract: This paper seeks to explore the attributes of a double-fed MIMO slot antenna, specifically designed with wireless local-area network (WLAN) frequency band filtering to enhance its applicability in ultra-wideband (UWB) communications. The antenna integrates a planar configuration comprising a pair of arc-shaped structures serving as radiation stubs, with a circular-ring slot and a shared ground plane. The arc-shaped stubs are equipped with Omega-shaped slots to generate the desired filtering notch. The antenna effectively operates within 3-10.7 GHz, providing UWB spectrum coverage. Furthermore, the antenna exhibits a singular and adjustable filtering characteristic, effectively suppressing interference from WLAN systems within the 5.5 GHz frequency.

articleTitle: Enhanced Multiple-Object Tracking in Video Using Hierarchical Kernel-Based Localization and Directional Histograms
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Future Telecommunications and Artificial Intelligence (IC-FTAI)
abstract: This paper proposes an improved method for multiple-object tracking in video using hierarchical kernel-based localization. First, all moving objects (e.g., hands, bodies) are detected in each frame. Next, object direction is determined by comparing histograms and distances with the previous frame, matching objects to kernels with similar characteristics. The method separates overlapping motion paths through kernel labeling. Performance metrics, including multiple objects tracking accuracy (MOTA) and precision (MOTP), validate the approach, with simulations showing faster and more accurate tracking than comparable methods.

articleTitle: Microstrip-Fed Monopole Antenna with Dual Notch Bands and Ultra-Wideband Features
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Future Telecommunications and Artificial Intelligence (IC-FTAI)
abstract: This research introduces a compact dual band-notched UWB antenna for wireless applications. It comprises a trapezoid patch with rotated L-shaped slits and an E-shaped slot, a modified/stepped rectangular feedline, and a trapezoid ground plane. The findings reveal that the antenna effectively operates within the 3–13 GHz frequency range, covering the UWB spectrum. Notably, two notched characteristics are achieved at 3.8 GHz and 5.5 GHz to mitigate interference from WLAN and WiMAX. The overall performance and key parameters of the antenna is assessed, confirming its satisfactory frequency response, radiations, efficiency/gain levels. Therefore, it meets the essential requirements for modern UWB systems, offering a reliable solution for wireless communication advancements.

articleTitle: Beam-Steerable Antenna Array with Broadband and Compact Resonators for MM - Wave Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Future Telecommunications and Artificial Intelligence (IC-FTAI)
abstract: This paper explores the features of an innovative antenna design that incorporates low-profile and broadband resonators, specifically optimized for advanced fifth generation (5G) cellular communication systems. The proposed approach is straightforward and can be effectively integrated into the mainboard of future mobile devices. The design includes eight bow-tie-ring resonators with microstripline feeding, arranged in a 1 ×8 linear configuration on the top of a smartphone board. It operates from 22 GHz to 40 GHz, achieving a −10 dB reflection coefficient that encompasses several critical bands within the 5G spectrum. Beyond the simplicity of its design, this phased array antenna also emphasizes essential radiation characteristics, ensuring it meets the varied demands of next-generation networks.

articleTitle: Enhance AES S-Box with Tinker-Bell Chaotic Map
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Future Telecommunications and Artificial Intelligence (IC-FTAI)
abstract: Security techniques must be enhanced to combat emerging methods of data stealing. The substitution Box(S-Box) serves as the basis of the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) encryption techniques, and the algorithm security is increased by its well-designed. S-Boxes currently in use: the Standard S-Box (SS-Box), and the Dynamic S-Box (DS-Box). An effective design of S- Box can boost the security of the encryption algorithm. DS-Box was generated previously by first key Schedule Algorithm (KSA) only, then the RC4 algorithm was used to generate DS- Box. In present two DS- Boxes generated by RC4 implemented with Henon chaotic map (HCM) and Logistic chaotic maps (LCM) to build modified S-Boxes, one algorithm is presented: DS-Box using RC4 algorithm implemented with the Tinkerbelle chaotic map (TCM) and is dependent on both the key and the plaintext. Then compare this algorithm with previous work; DS-Box using KSA only, DS-Box using RC4 only, DS-Box using RC4 implemented with HCM, and DS-Box using RC4 implemented with LCM. The purpose of the paper is to illustrate the effectiveness of the suggested DS-Box with RC4 using the TCM. These five S-boxes give good results but since the proposed S-boxes depend on affine transformation (AT), complexity and periodicity are ensured. Additionally, security is increased by the use of RC4 in DS-Box with TCM. It increases the difficulty of linear and differential cryptanalysis.

articleTitle: 6G-Enabled IoT Networks Cyber Threat Prevention Using Generative AI
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Future Telecommunications and Artificial Intelligence (IC-FTAI)
abstract: In this paper, we present the applications of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAl) in preotecting 6G-enabled loT networks from different cyber threats. The paper shall leverage Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and federated learning, in order to propose a novel framework for detecting therefore mitigates sophisticated cyber-attacks in real-time. Internet of Things (loT) devices using 6G wireless networks shall provide opportunities for enhancing connectivity by enabling secured smart applications. However, these 6G advancements also introduce significant cybersecurity challenges which require robust threat prevention strategies. The proposed framework takes advantages of the inherent 6G capability, such as high data rates, low latency, and network slicing. It implemented a distributed, AI-driven security mechanism that adapts to evolving threats. The simulation results and it analysis, demonstrates the “effectiveness” of the proposed framework in preventing a wide range of cyber-attacks, such as phishing, malware, and denial-of-service (DoS) attacks. It also ensures the integrity, confidentiality, and availability of loT services. The results of this study demonstrate the integration of AI in next-generation wireless networks, and offer insights into the design of resilient and the application of adaptive cybersecurity solutions.

articleTitle: Low-Profile/Dual-Band Planar Phased Array Patch Antenna for THz Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Future Telecommunications and Artificial Intelligence (IC-FTAI)
abstract: This research presents a new 4x4 planar phased array antenna designed specifically to meet the evolving requirements of future 6G communications in the Terahertz (THz) frequency range. Each antenna element is uniquely configured, utilizing a low-profile coaxial-fed patch antenna that incorporates a rotated π-shaped slot. This innovative design enables dual-band functionality, allowing the antenna to operate effectively at both 1.5 THz and 3 THz frequencies. Furthermore, the array's fundamental characteristics demonstrate excellent radiation patterns, gain, and beam-steering capabilities, which are essential for supporting the demanding specifications of 6G technology.

articleTitle: Lane Detection Using Computer Vision Techniques in ADAS Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Future Telecommunications and Artificial Intelligence (IC-FTAI)
abstract: Lane detection is a critical component of Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) aimed at improving road safety. This paper introduces a real-time lane detection system using computer vision techniques implemented in Python with OpenCV. The system efficiently identifies lane markers in video feeds, classifies them as continuous or dashed, and determines the vehicle's position relative to the lane. Additionally, an audible warning system alerts the driver when the vehicle veers outside the lane. Extensive testing demonstrates the system's effectiveness in real-time operation. Potential future improvements include handling more complex road scenarios and environmental conditions through machine learning integration.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Study of Fractal Antenna Performance Characteristics through SRR Superstrate Integration for Next-Generation Wireless Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Future Telecommunications and Artificial Intelligence (IC-FTAI)
abstract: The rapid growth of fifth-generation (5G) communication networks needs for the development of highly effective antennas that can meet specific requirement, including small size, high gain, and broad bandwidth. In this research, a fractal antenna with a superstrate based on Split Ring Resonators (SRRs) is designed and analysed for sub-6 GHz 5G applications. The proposed design of antenna is operate at 5.65GHz, which consists of three layers separated by specific distance. The bottom layer is a ground plane, middle layer is fractal antenna and top layer consist of 3×3 SRR array as superstrate. The gain enhancement of single fractal antenna is achieved through the superstrate. According to parametric studies, a maximal gain of 9.7 dBi can be achieved by placing the superstrate 30 mm from the antenna. The antenna's performance has been investigated using S-parameters and radiation patterns, which demonstrate a -25 dB return loss at 5.65GHz and a -10dB bandwidth of 300 MHz. The proposed design effectively addresses the difficulties of attaining high gain and miniaturization of antenna, making it suitable for sub-6GHz next-generation 5G communication systems.

articleTitle: Orange Disease Detection Using Pretrained ResNet50 and LIME for Explainable AI
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Future Telecommunications and Artificial Intelligence (IC-FTAI)
abstract: This paper presents a method for detecting diseases in oranges using a pretrained ResNet50 model. The diseases targeted are citrus canker, black spot, and citrus greening, in addition to fresh oranges. The goal is to achieve high classification accuracy while making the model more explainable to humans by using LIME (Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations) for interpretability. The dataset consists of 991 training images and 99 test images, divided across the four categories. The model achieved a test accuracy of 96.97%, a test loss of 3.6373, and a ROC AUC score of 0.978..

articleTitle: Lung Cancer Detection: The Role of Transfer Learning in Medical Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Future Telecommunications and Artificial Intelligence (IC-FTAI)
abstract: Lung cancer is a major global health issue, and improved patient results and treatment efficacy rely on early diagnosis. For many human diseases, including lung cancer, computer-aided detection (CAD) systems have greatly improved clinical analysis and decision-making. This study applies pre-trained deep learning techniques with a focus on transfer learning approaches and utilizes the available computed tomography (CT) scan image dataset (IQOTH/ NCCD) to investigate the automation of lung cancer detection through CT scans. It concentrates on the training and evaluation of VGG16, ResNet50V2, and InceptionV3 architecture using this dataset. The aim is to automate lung cancer identification, ultimately improving the accuracy of diagnosis and prognosis of the patient. The findings revealed ResNet50V2 is superior with impressive 98% accuracy, high sensitivity (95%) and excellent specification (99%). This investigation highlights how CAD systems can greatly improve the diagnostic process by providing radiologists with reliable tools to identify cancerous nodules, thereby reducing the risk of missed diagnosis.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Rectangular Microstrip Patch Antenna on Varied Substrates for RF Energy Harvesting Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Future Telecommunications and Artificial Intelligence (IC-FTAI)
abstract: In this paper, a 4-element rectangular microstrip patch antenna operating at 2.4 GHz has been introduced. The initial proposed antenna design is designed on an FR4 substrate with a relative dielectric permittivity of 4.4, featuring a patch dimension of 43.1 x 28.47 mm. To enhance efficiency, the proposed design was subsequently optimized using two different Roger materials as a substrate: R3003 with a permittivity of 3, and R5880 with a permittivity of 2.2. The study examines how variations in substrate material affect the antenna properties such as physical dimension, impedance matching radiation pattern and overall performance. The comparative analysis indicated that the S11 parameters achieve the best impedance matching at 2.402 GHz with R5880, followed by FR4 and R3003. The VSWR analysis further supports R5880 as the optimal material for efficient power transmission at this frequency. Additionally, far-field performance metrics such as efficiency, directivity, and gain are evaluated, revealing that the antenna with the R5880 substrate offers the best performance. This study focused on showing the impact of substrate material selection on design and properties.

articleTitle: A Compact Design of Phased Array Antenna with Folded Dipole Radiators for THz Communications and 6G Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Future Telecommunications and Artificial Intelligence (IC-FTAI)
abstract: This paper explores the characteristics of an innovative linear phased array designed to provide high gain and steerable radiation patterns, tailored of upcoming 6G networks. The array features a schematic with eight folded dipole elements arranged in a 1×8 linear format. These compact folded dipole resonators utilize microstrip-line feeds, optimizing their design. The proposed linear phased array achieves an impedance bandwidth of 1.85 to over 2.15 THz at −10 dB, delivering radiation gains exceeding 10 dBi across various frequencies and angles within its operational bandwidth. This performance meets the antenna design requirements for 6G networks and THz communications.

articleTitle: Relay Satellites for High Throughput Transmission in Earth Observation Missions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Future Telecommunications and Artificial Intelligence (IC-FTAI)
abstract: Research proposals to utilize relay satellites for high-throughput transmission in earth observation (EO) missions have attracted significant interest in recent years. Relay satellites can increase communication time windows between EO satellites and ground stations (GS). In particular, Walker Delta (WD) satellite constellations in medium-earth orbit (MEO) can keep persistent inter-satellite links at specific altitudes and inclinations. As such, WD relay satellites in MEO can enhance the overall throughput for EO missions. The capacity analysis of relay satellites in MEO will be of interest in practice. In this work, we present capacity analysis across four scenarios: (1) a direct link between low-earth orbit satellite and GS, (2) using a geosynchronous orbit (GEO) relay satellite, (3) using WD 3/3/0 relay constellation in MEO, and (4) using WD 4/2/1 relay constellation in MEO. We analyze the systems throughput using MATLAB and Systems Tool Kit and generate the required design curves. The obtained numerical results show that the WD 4/2/1 relay constellation has superior throughput and access durations. As such, it can deliver the highest average number of daily images to the GS.

articleTitle: Effect of Adopting Indoor Positioning on Wi-Fi System Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Future Telecommunications and Artificial Intelligence (IC-FTAI)
abstract: Recently, a new Indoor Positioning System (IPS) was introduced. It is based on establishing two orthogonal phased antenna arrays to target a specific location at any point in time. To enable simultaneous data transfer through the original Wi-Fi Access Point (AP) functionality, this paper proposes a new Space-Division Multiple Access (SDMA) scheme. Several aspects of a simulation utility have been added to accommodate the structure of the specific wave transmission. Limited simulation analysis is included to start evaluating data throughput in addition to lost MAC frames and compare them with the baseline of the conventional Carrier-Sense Multiple Access (CSMA) in Wi-Fi, The paper discusses findings from two simulation scenarios, conventional Wi-Fi system, as a benchmark, and combined SDMA/CSMA Wi-Fi, regarding a Wi-Fi communication system. The intent of the comparison is to measure the data throughput in the presence of IPS. Surprisingly, the comparison reveals that the throughput in the second scenario is double that of the first scenario. Moreover, the lost MAC frames are seen to be less in the second scenario than those of the first scenario, highlighting the effectiveness of the new IPS technique. With future study underway of including a variety of practical conditions in terms of the random number of stations in the indoor hall as well as different hall layouts and dimensions, the data throughput in addition to the lost frames enhancement/ degradation is yet to be determined.

articleTitle: Low Cost High Accuracy Moving Target Detection Filter Bank
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Future Telecommunications and Artificial Intelligence (IC-FTAI)
abstract: In radar and communication systems, accurate Doppler detection is essential for identifying the relative velocity of moving targets. This paper presents a novel, cost-effective filter bank design tailored to improve Doppler detection accu-racy. The proposed approach focuses on optimizing the signal processing chain to enhance target detection while maintaining low hardware complexity. By leveraging an adaptive filter bank architecture, this design achieves significantly higher frequency resolution and reduced computational overhead compared to conventional approaches. Simulation and hardware implemen-tation results demonstrate the design's robustness under varying operational conditions. These results validate its potential as a practical solution for real-time Doppler detection applications.

articleTitle: An Approach Using Deep Neural Networks for the Binary Classification of Mild Cognitive Impairment in Alzheimer's Disease: Early and Late Stages
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Future Telecommunications and Artificial Intelligence (IC-FTAI)
abstract: Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI) refers to the intermediate stage between normal brain function and the more severe decline caused by dementia. Alzheimer's Disease (AD) is a significant cause of dementia. Early detection of MCI can be beneficial for detecting individuals who exhibit the initial signs of AD. The AD Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) utilized Positron Emission Tomography (PET) images to diagnose MCI. MCI can be classified into two distinct categories: Early MCI (EMCI) and Late MCI (LMCI). In this study, a Deep Learning (DL) method was deployed with a limited number of PET images for binary classification of the two subcategories of MCI in AD patients. A total of 377 patients participated in this study, including 222 patients diagnosed with EMCI and 155 patients diagnosed with LMCI. The results indicated that the proposed Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model reached a validation accuracy of 99.26%, a training accuracy of 98.68%, and a testing accuracy of 99.26%. The model has exceptional classification capabilities, highlighting its ability to accurately distinguish between the EMCI and LMCI classes with minimal misclassifications.

Author Keywords: Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI), Alzheimer's disease (AD), Positron emission tomography (PET), Deep learning, Convolutional neural network (CNN), Neurological disease management Mild cognitive impairment (MCI)

articleTitle: CPW-Fed Monopole Antenna Design with Extended Operation Ultra-Wideband Band for Breast Cancer Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Future Telecommunications and Artificial Intelligence (IC-FTAI)
abstract: In this paper, a coplanar waveguide-fed (CPW-Fed) Ultra-Wideband Band antenna design is presented for the early detection of tiny tumors or cells in the human breast. The proposed antenna design configuration includes a modified circular radiation patch with a hexagonal slot and a half-oval-shaped ground plane arranged as a single layer. The antenna is designed on a low-cost FR4 substrate material with a loss tangent of 0.02, a dielectric constant of 4.4, and a thickness of 1.6 mm. It is compact with a size of 31.8x26x1. 6 mm3. The antenna operates at frequencies 2.8 GHz to 20 GHz, covering both microwave and millimeter spectra, with a fractional bandwidth of 150.8%. The proposed antenna offers over 98% radiation efficiency and 95% total efficiency, with maximum gain characteristics ranging from 1.5 to 5 dBi. The antenna is used to detect minuscule single and multiple tumors in a heterogeneous breast phantom, with results showing accurate detection of tumors of varying sizes, namely 5, 3.5 down to 2 mm. It emits radiation in all directions and conforms to a specific absorption rate (SAR) figure of merit limit specified by the Federal Communication Commission. The antenna design is validated through simulation using the CST STUDIO platform, and the results are compared to those of other available techniques in the literature. It is found to have comparable characteristics in addition to its ability to detect tiny tumors in the human breast.

articleTitle: Comparative Evaluation of Neural Network Models for Optimal Computational Offloading in Mobile Edge Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Future Telecommunications and Artificial Intelligence (IC-FTAI)
abstract: Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) has been promising in reducing latency for computational offloading to nearby edge servers and enhancing user experience. However, selecting the most suitable Machine Learning (ML) method for optimal task-offloading decisions remains a chal-lenge. This study proposes the most effective Neural Network Model (NNM) for making optimal offloading decisions. It has conducted a comparative analysis of several NNMs based on their performance metrics. The simulation results demonstrate that the Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) delivers the best performance by achieving the accuracy of 95.71 %, including other parameter metrices.

articleTitle: Intelligent Smart Home System: Secure Solution for Enhanced Efficiency and Comfort
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Future Telecommunications and Artificial Intelligence (IC-FTAI)
abstract: The smart home systems era has impressively advanced in the last decade, influencing many aspects in terms of security, efficiency, and ease. This paper presents a smart home security system that is a state of the art designed using TinkerCad for designing the circuitry and using Arduino IDE to implement code. The system combines door alarms, face recognition, automatic lighting, weather-based fan control, and Bluetooth remote control. We contribute to solving the challenges in integrating the low-power technology with strong security features, hence ensuring enhanced protection while guaranteeing energy efficiency. This work makes a comparison between our system and existing solutions, establishing improved functionality, energy consumption, and reliability.

articleTitle: Hybrid Iris Recognition: Leveraging HOG Features and Dense Networks for Enhanced Biometric Accuracy
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Future Telecommunications and Artificial Intelligence (IC-FTAI)
abstract: The article describes a new method for iris recognition, based on a hybrid approach combining edge detection, Histogram of Oriented Gradients (HOG) features, and dense neural networks(DNN), enabling improved accuracy and reduced training time. Using Circular Hough Transform (CHT)segmentation and Canny Edge Detection for localization, followed by feature extraction through HOG, the authors train the data using dense networks. The results show a 92.37% accuracy on the CASIA-Iris-Interval dataset and 96.28% on the IITD dataset, outperforming previous techniques. The authors illustrate the proposed method with results from MATLAB simulations on three datasets. The hybrid method allows for a reduction in training time by 10 minutes compared to traditional Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)methods. The effectiveness of the new method is confirmed by accuracy improvements of up to 5 %. These research results supplement existing iris recognition techniques and can be used for real-time biometric applications. The novelty and scientific contribution lie in integrating HOG and dense networks, enhancing both accuracy and computational efficiency in biometric systems.

articleTitle: Resource Allocation in Cognitive Radio Networks: A Comprehensive Review
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Future Telecommunications and Artificial Intelligence (IC-FTAI)
abstract: Cognitive radio (CR) technology has emerged as a promising solution to address the spectrum scarcity problem by enabling opportunistic access to underutilized frequency bands. Effective resource allocation plays a pivotal role in optimizing spectrum utilization and ensuring efficient coexistence between primary and secondary users. This comprehensive review delves into the intricacies of resource allocation techniques in cognitive radio networks, exploring both theoretical foundations and practical implementations. The review covers various models, optimization objectives, challenges, recent advances, and future directions, providing valuable insights for researchers, practitioners, and policymakers.

articleTitle: Early Lung Cancer Detection with a Fusion of Inception V3and Vision Transformers: A Binary Classification Study
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Future Telecommunications and Artificial Intelligence (IC-FTAI)
abstract: Lung cancer is a significant global health issue, causing around 13 % of newly diagnosed cancer cases and roughly 20% of cancer-related deaths. This study evaluates the relative efficacy of two advanced deep learning models, Vision Transformer (ViT) and Inception V3, in the classification of lung cancer using a publicly accessible dataset of MRI scans. The ViT model achieved a high training accuracy of 98% but struggled with generalization, stabilizing at around 77% validation accuracy due to potential overfitting. In contrast, the Inception V3 model, employing a transfer learning approach with frozen base layers, achieved a consistent enhancement in validation accuracy of 85.8% with a diminished validation loss of 0.3457. Metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and the area under the ROC curve are used to provide a comprehensive view of a model's effectiveness, thus better reflecting its performance across all classes. Overall, the Inception V3 model shows greater reliability in processing new input, underscoring the importance of model selection in developing effective AI-driven diagnostic tools for lung cancer.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Heart Disease Classification Based on Traditional and Ensemble Models
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Future Telecommunications and Artificial Intelligence (IC-FTAI)
abstract: Heart disease poses a serious and significant risk to human health. Timely and accurate diagnosis is essential for effective prevention and treatment, which can greatly reduce mortality rates. Traditional diagnostic methods often face limitations in accuracy and scalability, highlighting the need for advanced computational approaches. Machine learning has emerged as a powerful tool to address these challenges by analyzing complex patterns in medical data. In this paper, we propose a novel model combining various machine learning techniques to enhance the detection of heart disease. Our approach focuses on creating a robust training dataset through comprehensive data gathering, preprocessing, and transformation, integrating data from multi-ple sources: Cleveland, Long Beach VA, Switzerland, Hungarian, and Statlog datasets. We developed hybrid classifiers, including AdaBoost, AbaBoost Bagging Method (ABBM), Gradient Boost, Random Forest, Random Forest Bagging Method (RFBM), Majority Voting, XGB classifier, and Stacked Generalization. These were built by integrating conventional classifiers with advanced bagging and boosting techniques to improve prediction performance. Evaluation metrics such as Accuracy, Sensitivity, Precision, and Fl-Score were employed to rigorously assess the models. Among these, the proposed Stacked Generalization model demonstrated superior performance, achieving the highest accuracy of 95.38 %. The findings underscore the model's potential in effectively identifying individuals at risk of heart disease, offering a significant contribution to early detection and public health initiatives.

articleTitle: Enhanced Binary Chimp Optimization For Multiple Topology Error Detection and Identification in Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Future Telecommunications and Artificial Intelligence (IC-FTAI)
abstract: Topology errors pose significant challenges to state estimation and subsequent processes in power systems. While numerous techniques for detecting and identifying these errors have been explored in the literature, the majority focus on single topology error scenarios. In contrast, this paper proposes an optimization-based approach that not only improves detection accuracy but also effectively manages multiple topology errors. The study introduces two binary optimization techniques-the binary grey wolf algorithm and an enhanced version of the binary chimp algorithm. These methods are evaluated and compared for their performance and accuracy in detecting and identifying topology errors. To demonstrate their effectiveness, both algorithms were tested on the IEEE 57 bus system, showcasing their robust capabilities in accurately identifying a range of topology error cases.

Author Keywords: optimization- based topology errors detection and identification techniques

articleTitle: Smart IoT-Based Shared Bike System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Future Telecommunications and Artificial Intelligence (IC-FTAI)
abstract: With Egypt's residential districts and gated communities growing at an exponential rate, the issue of transportation within them has gained increased attention. Most of these gated areas lack any transportation options other than private cars, challenging eco-friendly mobility. This work presents a smart shared-bike system that offers a practical and affordable short-distance mobility option for places with limited transit options. The system promotes green and light transportation, aiming to decrease the carbon footprint by replacing pollutive vehicles with bikes. It is structured into three modules: a hardware module integrating embedded Linux with loT on a Raspberry Pi for data collection and an anti-theft module, a mobile application developed in Flutter for user interactions, and a web application serving as an admin panel for monitoring. Features include a smart lock for bike access, GPS for bike tracking, an accelerometer for detecting theft attempts, and real-time data transmission to Firebase. The implementation of this smart shared-bike system not only addresses transportation challenges in Egyptian residential areas but also offers economic advantages and supports sustainable mobility solutions.

articleTitle: Hybrid Approach Using LSTM Neural Networks and Whale Optimization Algorithm For Enhancing Depression Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Future Telecommunications and Artificial Intelligence (IC-FTAI)
abstract: Depression is a prevalent mental disorder, and accurate diagnosis is essential for effective intervention by proposing a novel approach for diagnosing depression using Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural networks combined with swarm intelligence algorithms. Accordingly, this research pays major attention to how the strength of LSTM in sequential data and optimization performance through swarm intelligence enhance the accuracy and reliability of the diagnosis of depression. So far, we utilized the Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA) algorithm for the optimal tuning of the model parameters of LSTM toward their optimal performance. The experimental results confirm the effectiveness of our approach, where the proposed model has an RMSE value of 3.75 and an MAE value of 3.15. These results indicate a higher performance compared to state-of-the-art methods and offer great potential for LSTMs combined with the WOA algorithm in the accurate diagnosis of depression. This may be a signal that the hybrid approach will serve perfectly in a clinical setting by allowing clinicians to identify depression among patients more precisely and reliably.

articleTitle: The Efficiency of Medical Diagnostic Robots in the Light of Legal Liability
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Future Telecommunications and Artificial Intelligence (IC-FTAI)
abstract: Robots in medical diagnostics assist healthcare personnel by boosting precision, speed, and consistency in processing patient data, ultimately supporting early and precise detection of diseases. These robotic devices frequently use AI and machine learning algorithms to interpret complex medical data and improve diagnostic findings. A robot entitled “Dr. HEMA: Horus Expert Medical Assistant” Robot is presented in this paper to assist medical personnel in the diagnosis of chronic diseases with an accuracy of 98.8% and an accuracy of 85% in predicting the severity of chronic diseases. Given the increasing use of artificial intelligence systems, especially smart robots, in various fields, there are concerns about the potential harm they may cause to others. Therefore, it is essential to address these issues to understand the extent to which civil liability is established for damages caused by smart robots and, consequently, the compensation for these damages. The regulations for protecting sensitive medical personal data in the context of a newly established right to health must be taken into consideration. To establish a legal basis for liability for damages caused by intelligent robots, it has been proposed to grant them legal personality. However, this proposal has not been universally agreed upon, as opinions differ regarding the granting of legal personality to intelligent robots. Some support the idea, while others oppose it. Throughout this paper, HEMA's diagnostic ability is traced within the frame of legal liability.

articleTitle: A Novel Approach to Speech Emotion Recognition Using Wav2Vec2
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Future Telecommunications and Artificial Intelligence (IC-FTAI)
abstract: Speech Emotion Recognition (SER), which allows computers to precisely understand and react to human emotions, is essential for improving human-computer interaction. This subject is crucial because it has the potential to significantly improve the user experience in applications including education and e-Iearning, mental health, customer service, Automotive Industry, and others. Speech Emotion Recognition (SER) systems that used classic machine learning techniques usually extract handcrafted audio features such as pitch, loudness, energy, spectral flux, and others each of which captured a distinct part of the emotional tone in speech. Despite their ease of use and interpretability, traditional machine learning models such as Support Vector Machines (SVMs) and Decision Trees frequently had trouble handling complex emotional patterns and speaker variances. These limitations led researchers to use deep learning models, specifically Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), which could analyze speech as a sequence and capture some temporal relationships. By simulating the evolution of emotions over time, RNN s improved emotion identification. However, RNNs faced their own limitations, particularly in handling long-range dependencies and in maintaining performance when faced with diverse emotional expressions or noisy environments. These challenges led to the Transformer models. Unlike previous models, Transformers can capture long-range dependencies and complex patterns in data, making them well-suited for capturing the nuanced expressions necessary for accurate emotion detection. Therefore, in this research, we will present a Wav2Vec2 transformer SER system that has been optimized on emotional speech data to recognize a variety of emotional states. We conducted our experiment on the small dataset called Ryerson Audio-Visual Database of Emotional Speech and Song (RA VDESS) and achieved an improvement in accuracy and robustness over previous methods. It achieved a testing accuracy of 89% when compared to SVM using GWO optimizer, which achieved an accuracy of 76%, and the LSTM using GWO optimizer, which achieved an accuracy of 71 %.

articleTitle: Dynamic Channel Reservation in Cognitive Radio Networks Using AI Driven SDN Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Future Telecommunications and Artificial Intelligence (IC-FTAI)
abstract: In cognitive radio networks (CRNs), secondary users (SUs) are permitted transmission access by using licensed channels previously assigned to primary users (PUs). Dynamic Spectrum Access (DSA) and spectrum sharing contribute to enhancing cooperative communications for PUs. Considering the scarcity of spectrum resources, extensive research attention has been dedicated to dynamic bandwidth allocation in recent years. In CRNs, dynamic channel reservation (DCR) improves network efficiency by optimizing the number of reserved channels. This paper proposes a centralized approach to DCR using a software-defined network (SDN) integrated with an artificial intelligence (AI) model. The proposed AI model employs a neural network architecture trained on historical network data to predict and manage channel allocation in real time. Key inputs to the model include PU and SU arrival rates, channel failure, and repair rates, enabling it to adaptively allocate reserved (R-CRN) and non-reserved channels (N-CRN) to balance PU channel availability and retainability while maintaining reliable access for SUs. The AI-driven controller reduces operational complexity and dynamically optimizes resource allocation, even in the presence of varying network conditions and failures. Simulation results demonstrate that this approach reduces PU blocking probability by up to 15% and lowers operational costs by 10%, while improving Quality of Service (QoS) metrics such as throughput and channel utilization. These quantifiable improvements highlight the adaptability and efficiency of the proposed solution, positioning it as a robust method for future spectrum management in CRNs.
